title: Full stomach, hidden hunger: seeing the real food problem

say: Full stomach, hidden hunger: seeing the real food problem.
This is the video for module one of Community Nutrition and Food Security.
A child can eat three times a day and still be malnourished. If every meal is mostly garri, white rice or pap, the stomach is full but the body is missing protein, iron, vitamin A, zinc and iodine.

panel.heading: Enough food is not the right food

Stomach full, body still missing nutrients
This is called hidden hunger
The answer is more variety

say: Food security has four parts. Availability asks: is the food there at all? For example, vegetables are scarce in the dry season.

panel.heading: The four pillars
items: Availability: is the food there at all?
Access: can the family get it?
Utilisation: does the body use it well?
Stability: is it steady all year?

say: Access asks: can the family get it? Beans may be in the market, but the family cannot afford them this month.

say: Utilisation is often forgotten. Dirty water causes repeated diarrhoea, so the child loses nutrients. Clean water, handwashing and fair sharing decide whether food becomes nutrition.

say: Stability asks: does food last through the year and through shocks, like sudden price jumps?

say: Stunting means too short for age. It builds slowly from months of poor diet and illness, and is hard to reverse after about age two. That is why the first 1,000 days, from pregnancy to age two, matter most.

cards.d: Too short for age. Builds slowly from poor diet and repeated illness. Hard to reverse after about age two.
Too thin for height. Can develop quickly after illness or food shortage, and is dangerous.
Lack of iron, vitamin A, iodine or zinc, even when weight looks fine.

say: Wasting means too thin for height. It can come quickly after illness or food shortage, and severe wasting needs urgent treatment.

cards.d: Too short for age. Builds slowly from poor diet and repeated illness. Hard to reverse after about age two.

say: Micronutrient deficiency, or hidden hunger, can be there even when weight looks fine.
Poor diet and infection feed each other in a cycle. So water, hygiene, vaccination and quick treatment are part of nutrition too.

say: Know these danger signs. A child who is very thin, has swelling of both feet, refuses to eat or drink, is unusually sleepy, or has diarrhoea with signs of dehydration needs a health facility the same day.
Food advice is not a substitute for treatment.

panel.heading: Go to a clinic the same day if
items: The child is very thin
Both feet are swollen
Refuses to eat or drink
Unusually sleepy
Diarrhoea with signs of dehydration

say: When money is tight, compare foods by what they give the body, not by the price per bag.
Ngozi's example prices are 3,000 naira for 1 kg of beans, 3,200 for 1 kg of groundnuts, and 7,500 for a crate of 30 eggs. Prices change, so use your own.

card.title: Cost per gram of protein
card.note: Example naira prices; check your own market.

say: Beans give about 230 g of protein, so each gram costs about 13 naira. Groundnuts come to about 12.8 naira.

card.title: Cost per gram of protein
card.note: Example naira prices; check your own market.

say: Eggs cost about 42 naira per gram. But eggs give vitamin A and very high quality protein, and are easy to feed a baby.
So Ngozi makes beans and groundnuts the daily base, and buys a few eggs for her one-year-old and her pregnant sister.

say: For example, Amina scored 5 out of 10, just at the target. Adding ugu to her stew and a slice of ripe pawpaw would lift her to 7 at little cost.

say: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron from beans and leaves, so eat orange, guava or tomato with the meal. Take tea and coffee between meals.

panel.heading: Small habits, big gains
items: Eat vitamin C foods with beans and leaves
Keep tea and coffee away from meals
Add ugu or efo near the end of cooking
Use iodised salt, kept covered
Cut sugary drinks first

say: Add leafy vegetables near the end of cooking, because long boiling loses vitamin C. Keep iodised salt covered and away from heat.

say: And sugary drinks and packaged snacks eat a surprising share of the budget. Cut them first to pay for beans and leaves.

Compare protein foods by cost per gram, and aim for at least 5 food groups a day.
